new.title: Climb the 546 steps to Afyon Castle
new.desc: The Karahisar fortress crowns a volcanic rock about 226 m above town and gave the city its 'Black Castle' name. Hittite, Phrygian and Seljuk rulers held it, and the Ottomans took it in 1392.
new.tip: Start from the path beside the Ulu Cami and go in the evening for the view over the town. Wear proper shoes: the steps are steep.
new.q: Afyon Kalesi, Tacı Ahmet, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Step into the wooden-columned Afyon Ulu Cami
new.desc: Built in 1272 under the Seljuks, this mosque holds a forest of 40 wooden columns with stalactite capitals under a nine-nave roof. It is on UNESCO's 2023 list of the wooden hypostyle mosques of medieval Anatolia.
new.tip: Remove shoes and keep clear of prayer times. The castle path starts right beside it.
new.q: Afyon Ulu Cami, Tacı Ahmet, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Meet the whirling dervishes at the Sultan Divani Mevlevihane
new.desc: This Mevlevi lodge, first built in the 14th century, is now a museum that recreates dervish daily life with displays and an audio guide. It is also known as the Mevlevi Türbe Camii.
new.tip: Allow about an hour. The lodge and its courtyard are in the old town below the castle.
new.q: Sultan Divani Mevlevihanesi Müzesi, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Browse Phrygian and Roman finds at the Afyon Archaeology Museum
new.desc: The museum shows finds from Afyonkarahisar and its surroundings from the Chalcolithic onwards. Phrygian, Roman and Byzantine statues, inscriptions and mosaics are the highlights. It moved to its current building at the Konya road junction in 1971.
new.tip: Combine it with a Frig Valley day trip so the carved rock monuments make sense. Check opening days beforehand.
new.q: Afyon Arkeoloji Müzesi, Dumlupınar Bulvarı, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: See the Gedik Ahmet Paşa Imaret Mosque
new.desc: Gedik Ahmed Pasha, a general and admiral under Mehmed II, built this complex in 1472 to celebrate a victory. It included an imaret soup kitchen, and the adjoining hamam still has its original stone basins.
new.tip: Visit with the Ulu Cami and the castle path; the hamam next door can still be used.
new.q: Gedik Ahmet Paşa Camii, Dairecep, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Admire the 17th-century Taşhan caravanserai
new.desc: Taşhan is a 17th-century inn in the middle of Afyon's old bazaar, opposite the Bedesten. It is one of several Ottoman han buildings in the old town.
new.tip: Walk in from the Uzun Çarşı side; the courtyard is quiet in the morning.
new.q: Taşhan, Uzun Çarşı, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Stand on Kocatepe where the 1922 offensive began
new.desc: Kocatepe lies in the Başkomutan Historical National Park, with the Büyük Taarruz Martyrs' Cemetery, the Kocatepe Monument and a Mustafa Kemal statue. The Great Offensive of August 1922 started here.
new.tip: Plan an hour and visit on or near 26 August when ceremonies are held. The site is outdoors and open in all weather.
new.q: Kocatepe Anıtı, Kocatepe, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Explore the rock-cut churches and tombs of Ayazini
new.desc: Ayazini is a village in the Phrygian Valley known for rock-carved dwellings, churches and tombs left by several civilizations. The church at the entrance of the village stands out for its carved facade.
new.tip: Go by car and allow two hours. Stout shoes help for scrambling over the rocks.
new.q: Ayazini, İhsaniye, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Look at the Döğer caravanserai on the Phrygian Way
new.desc: Döğer is among the caravanserais of Afyon's Phrygian Valley road. The town also sits close to the Kibele rock monuments Aslankaya and Kapıkaya.
new.tip: Combine it with Emre Lake and the Aslankaya monument in one loop; there is little lodging so day trips by car work best.
new.q: Döğer Kervansarayı, Döğer, İhsaniye, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Eat kaymaklı ekmek kadayıfı at Kaymakçızade
new.desc: Afyon's buffalo-milk kaymak has a geographical indication, and the city's best-known dessert is ekmek kadayıfı soaked in syrup and topped with thick kaymak. Kaymakçızade serves it on Basın Caddesi.
new.tip: Go for it as breakfast or an afternoon stop and share a plate; portions are rich.
new.q: Kaymakçızade, Basın Caddesi 3/A, Burmalı, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Try sucuk döner at Gamze Döner
new.desc: Afyon sucuk is a geographically protected product, and here it is stacked and sliced thin as a döner that stays crisp at the edges. An İskender version comes with butter sauce.
new.tip: Order the sucuk döner plain first, then the İskender if hungry.
new.q: Afyon Gamze Sucuk Döner, Milli Egemenlik Caddesi 6, Burmalı, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Taste kaymaklı lokum at Altınay Lokum
new.desc: Altınay sells Afyon lokum served with fresh kaymak and a winter-only kaymak dolması. The shop is on the Çevreyolu ring road.
new.tip: Buy a box to carry home and eat one fresh with kaymak in the shop.
new.q: Altınay Şekerleme & Lokum, Çevreyolu Bulvarı No:121/A, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Lunch on pastırmalı kuru fasulye at İkbal Lokantası
new.desc: İkbal is a historic bazaar lokanta known for beans with pastırma, Afyon tandır lamb and sucuk döner. The restaurant dates from 1922 and sits on Uzun Çarşı.
new.tip: Come at lunch when the daily pots are fresh; ask for bread and ayran with the beans.
new.q: İkbal Lokantası Uzun Çarşı, Millet Caddesi, Burmalı, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Order lamb tandır at Salim Usta
new.desc: This long-established bazaar lokanta serves lamb tandır, keşkek and zülbiye kebab. It opens early and also does a keşkek breakfast.
new.tip: Go early for keşkek, or at lunch for the tandır.
new.q: Salim Usta Uzun Çarşı, Millet Caddesi, Burmalı, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Eat göce köfte and Afyon kebabı at Musakka
new.desc: Musakka cooks on wood fire in copper pots and clay dishes. Its menu includes göce köftesi, keşkek, Afyon kebabı and a patlıcan böreği made without yufka.
new.tip: Share a few small plates to taste several of them.
new.q: Musakka Restaurant, Basın Caddesi 10, Burmalı, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Have haşhaşlı katmer for breakfast at Selvi Haşgeşli
new.desc: Afyon's poppy-seed pastries are the local breakfast, and Selvi Haşgeşli makes haşhaşlı katmer, mercimekli bükme and gözleme by hand. Kaymak and honey come on the side.
new.tip: Go for the katmer with kaymak and honey at breakfast time.
new.q: Selvi Haşgeşli Yöresel Lezzetler, Kılıç Ali Caddesi 7, Kasımpaşa, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Eat a köfte sandwich with yayık ayran at Köfteci İrfan
new.desc: Köfteci İrfan serves köfte in crusty bread with plenty of onion, with yayık ayran. It is on Basın Caddesi.
new.tip: Order a sandwich with ayran; a quick and cheap stop.
new.q: Köfteci İrfan, Basın Caddesi, Burmalı, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Scoop buffalo-milk ice cream at Hidayet Abi'nin Yeri
new.desc: This pastry shop makes fresh manda kaymak daily, kaymak plates and manda-milk ice cream.
new.tip: Try the ice cream with a spoon of kaymak.
new.q: Hidayet Abi'nin Yeri, Birlik Caddesi 2/A, Dairecep, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Have a village breakfast at Frigya Organik Köy Evi
new.desc: A family-run village house in the Frig Valley serves stone-oven bread, kaymak, cheeses and egg dishes.
new.tip: Pair it with a drive to Ayazini; call ahead for opening times.
new.q: Frigya Organik Köy Evi, Üçlerkayası, İhsaniye, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Soak in the Ömer-Gecek thermal waters
new.desc: Ömer-Gecek is one of Afyon's four declared thermal tourism centres, about 15 km from town on the Kütahya road. The Ömer and Gecek resorts together offer several hundred beds.
new.tip: Day passes are sold at several hotels; call to check prices.
new.q: Ömer Gecek Kaplıcaları, Afyonkarahisar Merkez, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Visit the ancient Hüdai thermal baths at Sandıklı
new.desc: The Sandıklı-Hüdai springs are said to date from the 3rd to 5th centuries AD and are one of Afyon's four thermal zones.
new.tip: Plan a day trip or stay overnight; Sandıklı is about 60 km from Afyon.
new.q: Hüdai Kaplıcaları, Sandıklı, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Wander the fairy chimneys of İscehisar
new.desc: İscehisar is a small marble town with fairy chimneys, described as a small Cappadocia. The Kırkinler rock settlement has a Byzantine church, chapel and tombs.
new.tip: Go in daylight and bring good shoes.
new.q: İscehisar Peribacaları, İscehisar, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Paddle or picnic by Emre Lake in the Phrygian Valley
new.desc: Emre Lake, near Döğer in İhsaniye, lies by Phrygian rock monuments and has been developed for canoeing and water sports. Pelicans visit the lake.
new.tip: Check locally about canoe hire; a pleasant stop on the Phrygian Way.
new.q: Emre Gölü, Döğer, İhsaniye, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Hike Göynüş Valley among the Phrygian rock monuments
new.desc: Göynüş Valley in İhsaniye has the Aslantaş, Yılantaş and Maltaş monuments, caves, rock settlements and churches from Roman and Byzantine times.
new.tip: Count on half a day with a car; carry water as there are few facilities.
new.q: Aslantaş Yılantaş Anıtı, Göynüş Vadisi, Kayıhan, İhsaniye, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Walk the İnceler Canyon near Sandıklı
new.desc: İnceler Canyon is a roughly 15 km canyon near Sandıklı with steep cliffs and clear water.
new.tip: Better in spring and early summer; bring water shoes.
new.q: İnceler Kanyonu, Sandıklı, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Hike Akdağ Nature Park above Sandıklı
new.desc: Akdağ was registered a nature park in 2000 and declared a national park in 2024.
new.tip: Go in late spring to autumn for hiking and picnics.
new.q: Akdağ Tabiat Parkı, Kocayayla, Sandıklı, Afyonkarahisar

new.title: Walk up to Kütahya Castle on Hisar Hill
new.desc: The Byzantine-rooted fortress above the city once had 72 towers according to Evliya Çelebi. It overlooks the whole old town.
new.tip: Go late afternoon for the views over the city.
new.q: Kütahya Kalesi, Hisar Tepesi, Kütahya Merkez, Kütahya

new.title: See Kütahya Ulu Cami with its Aizanoi columns
new.desc: The Great Mosque was completed in 1410 and later repaired by Mimar Sinan. Columns from Aizanoi were reused in the building.
new.tip: Look at the columns and the carved door; free entry.
new.q: Kütahya Ulu Camii, Kütahya Merkez, Kütahya

new.title: Trace Kütahya tiles at the Çini Museum
new.desc: The Tile Museum opened in March 1999 in the imaret of the Germiyan Bey II Yakub complex and holds about 500 Seljuk and Ottoman pieces.
new.tip: Go first to understand what you will see in the workshops later.
new.q: Kütahya Çini Müzesi, Germiyan, Kütahya Merkez, Kütahya

new.title: Visit the Kossuth House where Hungary's leader lived in exile
new.desc: Lajos Kossuth and about 56 refugees stayed in Kütahya in 1850-51 in this two-storey wooden house of seven rooms. It opened as a museum on 19 September 1982 with an 18th-century piano and Hungarian porcelain.
new.tip: Free entry; closed Mondays and hours vary by season.
new.q: Kossuth Evi Müzesi, Macar Sokak, Gediz Caddesi No:27, Kütahya Merkez, Kütahya

new.title: Visit the Kütahya Archaeology Museum in a 1314 madrasa
new.desc: The museum next to the Ulu Cami occupies a madrasa built in 1314 by Umur bin Savcı.
new.tip: Pair it with the Ulu Cami next door.
new.q: Kütahya Arkeoloji Müzesi, Kütahya Merkez, Kütahya

new.title: See Dönenler Mosque, the old Mevlevi lodge of Kütahya
new.desc: Dönenler was a Mevlevi lodge dating to the 14th century, closed after the 1925 ban on Sufi orders; its semahane hall is now used as a mosque.
new.tip: Look at the semahane from outside prayer times.
new.q: Dönenler Camii, Kütahya Merkez, Kütahya

new.title: Admire the tiled Çinili Cami
new.desc: A mosque in Kütahya decorated with tiles, listed as one of the city's best-known symbols.
new.tip: Visit with the nearby tile shops.
new.q: Çinili Cami, Kütahya Merkez, Kütahya

new.title: Watch tile painting at Mehmet Gürsoy's workshop
new.desc: Mehmet Gürsoy, named a UNESCO Living Human Treasure in 2009, runs a ceramic workshop on Germiyan Sokağı that also trains students.
new.tip: Call ahead; visiting hours are not posted.
new.q: Mehmet Gürsoy Çini Atölyesi, Germiyan Sokak, Kütahya Merkez, Kütahya

new.title: Eat cimcik in the old Germiyan Konağı
new.desc: Cimcik is Kütahya's local dumpling dish served with yoghurt and melted butter, and a restored Ottoman mansion on Germiyan Sokağı serves Kütahya dishes.
new.tip: Order cimcik with yoghurt.
new.q: Germiyan Konağı, Germiyan Sokağı, Kütahya Merkez, Kütahya

new.title: Stand beneath the Temple of Zeus at Aizanoi
new.desc: Begun under Domitian and finished under Hadrian, the temple is the best preserved Zeus temple in Anatolia. The site is on UNESCO's tentative list and also has a theatre, stadium and baths.
new.tip: Allow two hours; go early in summer.
new.q: Aizanoi Antik Kenti, Çavdarhisar, Kütahya

new.title: Visit Eğrigöz Castle, linked to Vlad the Impaler
new.desc: The castle on a hill east of Eğrigöz village is associated with Vlad the Impaler's 1442 stay as an Ottoman hostage.
new.tip: Remote; check road conditions first.
new.q: Eğrigöz Kalesi, Eğrigöz, Emet, Kütahya

new.title: Hike İkitaş Canyon near Eğrigöz
new.desc: İkitaş is a 7.6 km canyon near Eğrigöz being developed for tourism.
new.tip: Expect few facilities; go in dry weather.
new.q: İkitaş Kanyonu, Eğrigöz, Emet, Kütahya

new.title: Pay respects at the Dumlupınar Martyrs' Cemetery
new.desc: The cemetery opened on 30 August 1972 with the Milisler, Üç Komutan and Mehmetçik monuments; a museum sits in the former headquarters building.
new.tip: Open daily 08:30-17:30; ceremonies are held on 30 August.
new.q: Dumlupınar Şehitliği, Dumlupınar, Altıntaş, Kütahya

new.title: Soak at the Eynal thermal springs in Simav
new.desc: Eynal is a spa about 4 km from Simav at the foot of Gölcük mountain, mentioned by Evliya Çelebi, with a capacity of about 800 beds.
new.tip: Busy in school holidays.
new.q: Eynal Kaplıcaları, Simav, Kütahya

new.title: See the Babuk Bey mosque, a Germiyan relic in Simav
new.desc: The Babuk Bey complex was built in the early 1300s by a vizier of the Germiyan beylik; only the mosque survives.
new.tip: Short stop in town.
new.q: Babuk Bey Camii, Simav, Kütahya

new.title: Cross the 14th-century Dokuzgöz Bridge at Simav
new.desc: A Germiyan-era bridge that still stands though the stream it crossed has moved.
new.tip: Quick stop.
new.q: Dokuzgöz Köprüsü, Simav, Kütahya

new.title: See the Karun Treasure at the Uşak Archaeology Museum
new.desc: Founded in 1970, the museum is famous for the Karun Treasure of Lydian-Persian gold and silver from mounds near Güre, including a winged seahorse brooch.
new.tip: The second floor holds the treasure.
new.q: Uşak Arkeoloji Müzesi, Uşak Merkez, Uşak

new.title: Step onto the Ulubey Canyon glass terrace
new.desc: A 135 square metre glass terrace opened in 2015 above Ulubey Canyon, a 40-45 km long, 135-170 m deep canyon.
new.tip: Reported open 09:00-21:00; check the fee.
new.q: Ulubey Kanyonu Cam Teras, Ulubey, Uşak

new.title: Explore the ruins of Blaundus above Ulubey Canyon
new.desc: A Hellenistic-era city in Ulubey whose excavations have run since 2018.
new.tip: One listing says the site may be closed; check first.
new.q: Blaundus Antik Kenti, Ulubey, Uşak

new.title: Eat Uşak tarhana soup at Tarhana Baba
new.desc: Uşak tarhana is a geographically registered soup, fermented 21 days or more with lots of red pepper.
new.tip: Order with bread.
new.q: Tarhana Baba, Uşak Merkez, Uşak

new.title: Visit the Uşak Atatürk and Ethnography Museum
new.desc: A town museum listed among Uşak's sights.
new.tip: Check opening days.
new.q: Uşak Atatürk ve Etnografya Müzesi, Hisarkapı Uluyolu Sokak 75, Elmalıdere, Uşak Merkez, Uşak
